title: Chancellor Healey Delivers First Budget: Bank Tax Rise, £100 Energy Help, Fuel Duty Cut Extended
detail: Chancellor John Healey delivered his first Budget on 28 October 2026, the first of Andy Burnham's government. Measures included £100 of help with energy bills, a bank tax and gambling machine duty rise, an extension of the fuel duty cut to July 2027, a permanent 55p mileage allowance, a new Starter ISA with the £20,000 cash ISA limit retained, and £4.7bn for the Your First Home scheme. The House of Lords Library described the measures as relatively small in fiscal terms; the OBR forecast higher taxes, spending and borrowing than previously expected, with the fiscal rule met by a reduced £15bn margin.
